source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 7: Homo sapiens; genus, family, order, class and phylum; examples using Solanum, Panthera, Felis, Solanaceae, Felidae, Canidae, Carnivora, Primata and Mammalia.

questions.question: According to the page, what is the scientific name of human beings?
questions.explanation: The page states that humans belong to species sapiens in genus Homo, and the scientific name is Homo sapiens.
questions.source_text: The scientific name thus, for human being, is written as Homo sapiens.

questions.question: A genus comprises which group, according to the page?
questions.explanation: The page defines genus as a group of related species sharing more characters with one another than species of other genera.
questions.source_text: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera.

questions.question: Compared with species from other genera, species within one genus have:
options: Fewer shared characters in every case
questions.explanation: The page explains that related species in one genus share more characters with each other than species of other genera.
questions.source_text: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera.

questions.question: Which two organisms are given as different species belonging to the genus Solanum?
questions.explanation: The page says potato and brinjal are different species but both belong to Solanum.
questions.source_text: potato and brinjal are two different species but both belong to the genus Solanum.

questions.question: Which animals are identified on the page as species of genus Panthera?
questions.explanation: Lion, leopard and tiger are listed as species of Panthera; cats are placed in Felis in this passage.
questions.source_text: Lion (Panthera leo), leopard (P. pardus) and tiger (P. tigris) ... are all species of the genus Panthera.

questions.question: Which genus is described as including cats and differing from Panthera?
questions.explanation: The page says Panthera differs from Felis, which includes cats.
questions.source_text: This genus differs from another genus Felis which includes cats.

questions.question: A family consists of a group of related:
questions.explanation: The page describes family as the next category, containing related genera.
questions.source_text: Family, has a group of related genera

questions.question: Compared with genus and species, related genera in a family have:
questions.explanation: The text says families have fewer similarities than genus and species.
questions.source_text: a group of related genera with still less number of similarities as compared to genus and species.

questions.question: Plant families are characterised on the basis of which features, according to the page?
questions.explanation: The page specifies both vegetative and reproductive features of plant species.
questions.source_text: Families are characterised on the basis of both vegetative and reproductive features of plant species.

questions.question: Which genera are placed in the plant family Solanaceae in the example?
questions.explanation: The page names Solanum, Petunia and Datura as three genera in Solanaceae.
questions.source_text: three different genera Solanum, Petunia and Datura are placed in the family Solanaceae.

questions.question: Which pair of genera is placed together in the family Felidae in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage places Panthera and Felis in the family Felidae.
questions.source_text: genus Panthera, comprising lion, tiger, leopard is put along with genus, Felis (cats) in the family Felidae.

questions.question: According to the page, cats and dogs are separated into which families, respectively?
questions.explanation: The passage states that cats and dogs are separated into Felidae and Canidae, respectively.
questions.source_text: They are separated into two different families – Felidae and Canidae, respectively.

questions.question: An order is described as an assemblage of:
options: Families exhibiting a few similar characters
questions.explanation: The page defines order as a higher category made up of families with a few similar characters.
questions.source_text: Order being a higher category, is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters.

questions.question: According to the page, order and other higher taxonomic categories are generally identified based on:
questions.explanation: The passage says order and higher categories are identified based on aggregates of characters.
questions.source_text: Generally, order and other higher taxonomic categories are identified based on the aggregates of characters.

questions.question: Which order is given for the plant families Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae?
questions.explanation: The page places Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae in the order printed as Polymoniales, mainly based on floral characters.
questions.source_text: Plant families like Convolvulaceae, Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters.

questions.question: Which families are stated to be included in the animal order Carnivora?
questions.explanation: The page states that Carnivora includes Felidae and Canidae.
questions.source_text: The animal order, Carnivora, includes families like Felidae and Canidae.

questions.question: Which category includes related orders?
questions.explanation: The page defines class as a category that includes related orders.
questions.source_text: This category includes related orders.

questions.question: Which organisms or groups are mentioned as examples in the discussion of class Mammalia?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions monkey, gorilla and gibbon in order Primata, and tiger, cat and dog among animals in order Carnivora; these orders are placed in class Mammalia.
questions.source_text: order Primata comprising monkey, gorilla and gibbon is placed in class Mammalia along with order Carnivora that includes animals like tiger, cat and dog.

questions.question: The page says classes comprising fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals constitute which next higher category?
questions.explanation: The page introduces phylum as the next higher category above class for these animal groups.
questions.source_text: Classes comprising animals like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the next higher category called Phylum.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly moves from genus to family to order to class, as described across the examples on this page?
questions.explanation: The page presents family as the category above genus, order above family, and class as a category containing related orders.
questions.source_text: The next category, Family ... Order being a higher category ... This category includes related orders.
